author: kevaundray
content: <@439032863904628745>  / <@592004585506340885> checking the specs; are we only reducing the number of subnets and not the number of committees for pq-gasper?

author: kevaundray
content:
It seems like we only reduce the number of subnets to 16, which I think implies that there will still be 64 stark proofs to aggregate since there are 64 committees. 

Was this the intention?

author: jtraglia
content: Hmm yes, that is accurate. There would still be 64 committees. I forget who suggested lowering the number of subnets & what their rationale was. I believe they may have intended to change both the number of subnets & the committee size. But that's a pretty invasive change 🤔 it would involve changing the attestation container.

author: jtraglia
content: Maybe we should revert that & keep the `TARGET_AGGREGATORS_PER_COMMITTEE_PQ` reduction (from 16 to 4).

author: kevaundray
content:
I think we can work with multiple committees on a subnet, in this case 4 committees per subnet.

Each subnet would produce 4 proofs, 1 per committee. We could then do a 4 -> 1 to produce 1 proof with 4 separate committee bitlist in that subnet

author: kevaundray
content: This would mean that the number of proofs equals the number of subnets without changing the attestation container

author: jtraglia
content: Hmm I see. To be clear, only one (of the 4) proofs is chosen per committee, right?

author: jtraglia
content: This means there would be another aggregator role too.

author: jtraglia
content: Or who makes the subnet proof, with the 4 committee proofs.

author: kevaundray
content: yeah, if we have 4 aggregators per committee then only one of them would be chosen

author: kevaundray
content: I was thinking any of the 16 aggregators in that subnet could do it; 4 aggregators per committee and 4 committees in the subnet

author: kevaundray
content: I guess it would be good if we didn't have a bunch of these duplicated subnet proofs being sent to the global topic

author: jtraglia
content: That was going to be my next question.

author: jtraglia
content: I think Kamil had a "global proof topic" or something.

author: kevaundray
content: I think the only way to avoid redundancy, is if the aggregators for a particular subnet, agree on whats the best aggregate and then agree to only publish the best

author: jtraglia
content: Speaking of which, we might need to double check that it's safe to reduce the number of aggregators per committee. I just noticed this comment from Ben.

author: kevaundray
content: Yeah thats what I computed too, ie a 1.8 % chance that there is no aggregator for a committee with 4 aggregators

author: kevaundray
content: So thats about 36 committees per epoch on average

author: kevaundray
content:
I personally like the idea of making aggregator selection deterministic (so we use randao to select the aggregators)

 <@486501030046203915> mentioned it a few hours ago https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1569690422010191873/1570818162667032719, then instead of an expected value its an exact value (assuming the chosen aggregators are online)

author: jtraglia
content: Yep, something like that would be good.

author: kevaundray
content: Copy-pasting; if we use randao then feel free to use 8384 as inspiration (its the same for attester aggregators)
